title: SLO-driven Resilience Contracts: Retry Budgets, Hedging, Idempotency, and Regional Failover
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Standardize retry/timeouts/backoff across services and SDKs with explicit SLO-driven retry budgets, hedged request semantics, and a clear idempotency contract that works across multi-region failover and load-shedding scenarios. The goal is a single resilience contract that services and client SDKs implement to avoid cascading retries, ensure safe deduplication of mutating requests, and provide predictable cost/latency trade-offs for customers. This ticket covers: defining the contract, compatibility rules for hedged requests, idempotency key format and TTL, SDK APIs for retries and backoff configuration, and operational signals for load-shedding and regional failover.
technical_notes: Retry budget concept: per-route SLO expressed as p95 latency and error budget; derive per-request retry budget (max retries + hedged attempts) so aggregated retries don't violate downstream SLOs or provider cost goals.

Default client behavior: exponential backoff with jitter, base_backoff=50ms, max_backoff=2s, max_retries derived from route retry budget (default 2). SDKs expose an opt-in hedging API; hedges are allowed only for read or idempotent-safe endpoints unless explicit idempotency header is present.

Hedging policy: single hedged attempt after hedging_delay = min(50ms, 10% of route p95) when no response headers received and remaining retry budget allows; hedged attempts count against the same retry budget.

Idempotency key rules: header 'Idempotency-Key' (RFC 7231 extension) using a v4 UUID or customer-provided stable token; TTL default 24h for hosted API, pluggable for Private deployments. Services MUST deduplicate based on (idempotency-key, tenant-id, route, attempted-op-hash).

Cross-region considerations: idempotency dedupe must be served from a single canonical region for a given customer/route or via globally-consistent control-plane lease. For failover, SDKs include region_hint; when switching regions, SDK preserves Idempotency-Key and includes 'original-region' header so the server can consult global dedupe store if available.

Load-shedding: when resource pressure > configured threshold, service returns HTTP 429 with 'Retry-After' and 'X-Redwood-Retry-Budget' header exposing remaining retry budget; SDKs should surface a structured error with backoff recommendation and avoid immediate retries beyond budget.

Operational signals: routes must emit metrics: retries_sent, hedged_attempts, idempotency_hit_rate, dedupe_store_hits, shed_count, p95_latency, error_budget_remaining. Alerts: sustained hedged_attempt_rate > 5% and retry amplification > 1.5x should trigger SRE review.

Compatibility: deploy this contract via feature-flagged rollout in SDKs (JS, Python, Go, Java). Default to previous behavior but expose new APIs and opt-in hedging; runtime will enforce server-side budget limits.
Security: idempotency-key values treated as opaque; do not log keys in plaintext to long-term logs. Mark this change for a security review (KMS for dedupe store keys for Private deployments).
Docs & PRs: design doc in Confluence + SDK interface proposal before implementation PRs.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and approved by Platform SRE, API, and SDK leads (link to confluence).
Service-side implementation: common retry/hedge middleware that enforces per-route retry budgets and emits required metrics.
SDK changes: JS/Python/Go clients implement retry budget computation, expose hedging opt-in API, and surface structured 429 with retry budget header.
Integration tests: simulate multi-region failover path and verify deduplication across region switch when Idempotency-Key preserved.
Load-shedding behavior: under controlled overload, services return 429 with Retry-After and SDK stops further retries beyond budget and surfaces error to caller.
Backward compatibility: default behavior unchanged for existing customers until SDKs opt-in; rollout plan documented.
comments: 2025-02-13 - Kickoff: Alignment meeting with SRE, API, and SDK leads. Agreed on 'retry budget' as primary abstraction; Aisha to own design doc.
2025-02-20 - Decision: Hedging allowed by default only for safe/idempotent read endpoints. Mutating endpoints require explicit Idempotency-Key header to allow hedging/automatic retries.
2025-02-25 - PR feedback: runtime middleware should expose remaining_budget in response headers for better SDK decisioning (see PR #754). Marco to add header 'X-Redwood-Retry-Budget' to runtime.
2025-03-03 - SRE note: simulated load test showed 12% hedged attempts on heavy p95 spike; agreed to tighten hedging_delay default from 100ms -> 50ms and add circuit breaker tuning per-route.
2025-03-05 - SDK owners: JS and Python SDKs prototyped opt-in hedging API; awaiting integration tests for multi-region dedupe.
